jamie: FYI a mid-enterprise customer reported a sudden p99 jump for the hosted chat endpoint ~09:12 UTC. p95 up too. They saw timeouts on a few flows.

simon: I pulled metrics — host group us-west-2-prod-gpu3 shows p95 from 220ms -> 480ms and p99 from 1.1s -> 3.8s starting 09:10. Coincides with last night's kernel builds (flashopt=on) in the canary batch. :eyes:

maria: Do we have quick repro steps? If we can reproduce with a load test we can validate mitigations before touching prod.

jamie: Minimal repro I used locally: run 500 concurrent chat streams (seq ~1024, temperature 0.0) against hosted/stable-gpt-mid. Script below. Repro reliably shows p99 > 2s.
```bash
# repro (approx)
ab -n 2000 -c 500 -T 'application/json' -p payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
# payload.json contains a single short system+user that causes 1k token decode worst-case
```

simon: Logs show kernel selection debug in runtime: `kernel=flash_v2` picked for model=gpt-mid, compileflags: `flash_opt_level=2`. Sample log: 
```
[09:11:24] runtime/exec: model=gpt-mid shard=12 seq_len=1024 kernel=flash_v2 latency_ms=3845
[09:11:25] runtime/exec: model=gpt-mid shard=12 kernel=flash_v2 compile_hash=abc123
```

elaine: Quick mitigation we can do now: override kernel selection for that model/variant to `sdpa_fallback` at routing layer (no deploy needed). That should reduce tail latency while we investigate the compile flag regression.

maria: Steps to apply override (tested on staging):
```bash
# admin API (internal)
curl -s -X POST "https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/runtime/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"selector":{"model":"gpt-mid","variant":"stable"},"override":{"kernel":"sdpa_fallback","reason":"p99 spike 2026-03-17"}}'
# verify
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/runtime/overrides?model=gpt-mid" | jq
```

jamie: I can apply the override now. Recommend 100% for affected pool (us-west-2-prod-gpu3) then monitor for regressions. If green, we can roll to global.

simon: +1. Also pin a traffic split to the previous compiled build for an immediate rollback path: admin call to set `compile_hash` override to previous-known-good. That keeps flash enabled where it's stable.

deploy-bot: canary rollout: flash-compile-v2 -> 100% canary completed at 2026-03-16T23:50Z :white_check_mark: 

elaine: Post-mitigation investigation notes:
- capture full `nvprof` and kernel counters for failing requests (seq 1024).
- run microbenchmarks of flash_v2 vs sdpa_fallback for batch sizes 1-32 and seq 256/512/1024.
- check third-party dependency versions (cuBLAS/cuDNN/driver) that could change kernel perf.

maria: Action items: 1) jamie apply override and post timestamp, 2) simon run microbench & share perf table, 3) I'll prepare a short customer update template. I'll own postmortem if this is a release regression.

jamie: Applied override at 09:22 UTC to selector model=gpt-mid variant=stable for pool=us-west-2-prod-gpu3. Rolling p99 back to ~1.2s on initial checks. Will keep monitoring and post metrics in 15m. :thumbsup:

simon: Starting microbench now. Posting CSV in thread when done. If sdpa cost is significantly higher we may need a targeted routing rule (only seq>512) instead of global override.

elaine: Good call. Also add a runtime guard to auto-fallback on 3 consecutive p99 violations > 2s for a model/variant to avoid future customer impact. Filed a ticket: INF-9482.

jamie: Thanks team — will update customer and close the support escalation after 1h of stable metrics.

ops-bot: Escalation updated: status -> mitigated, owners -> jamie,maria,simon, ticket INF-9482 linked.
